title: Add rollback annotations and compact release-index generator for model onboarding
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes:
- Introduces rollback annotations to capture safe rollback points during model onboard flows.
- Adds a compact release-index generator that consolidates per-model changelogs into a single searchable index for faster release note assembly.
- Backward-compatible: existing release hooks continue to work; new index is additive.
description:
Motivation:
During several manual rollouts we observed that the model onboarding flow lacked a canonical, machine-readable marker for points where a rollout could safely be reverted. Simultaneously, assembling release notes for weekly model bundles is slow because we aggregate many per-model changelogs at publish time. This PR provides two ergonomic building blocks: (1) explicit rollback annotations emitted during onboarding (metadata + provenance), and (2) a compact release-index generator that aggregates and indexes changelog fragments for fast lookup and deterministic release-note generation.

What I changed (summary):
- Added the "rollback annotation" schema and lightweight emitter in onboard/processor/rollback_metadata.py. The emitter records a compact provenance blob (profile_id, profile_version, timestamp, trigger, rollback_hint) written to model metadata store and appended to release fragments.
- Implemented a compact indexer (release/indexer/compact_indexer.go) that consumes onboarding fragments and produces a single compressed JSONL index with per-model pointers and summary tags (semver-like stamps, perf delta buckets). The index is optimized for the console UI and the release-note assembler.
- Added a small shell recipe and CI step to generate and validate the index (scripts/release/generate_index.sh, release/recipes/compact_index_recipe.yaml).
- Documentation and a how-to (docs/onboard/release-index.md) describing consumption patterns and the rollback annotation semantics.
- Unit tests covering emitter behavior and indexer end-to-end (tests/onboard/test_rollback_annotations.py).

Commits (high level):
- 1a9f3c2: add rollback annotation schema and emitter
- b4e7d8a: implement compact indexer and indexing pipeline
- c2d5f11: add shell recipe and basic integration script
- d8f7a3b: docs and examples for release index consumption
- e4c1b90: add tests and CI integration; fix edge cases from review

Files changed (high level):
- onboard/processor/rollback_metadata.py: new emitter, 1:1 backwards compatible write to metadata store, emits lightweight provenance.
- release/indexer/compact_indexer.go: new indexer with an emphasis on compact keys and summary buckets; uses existing store clients.
- scripts/release/generate_index.sh: convenience wrapper used by CI and release automation.
- docs/onboard/release-index.md: guidance + examples.
- tests/onboard/test_rollback_annotations.py: unit tests + small integration harness.

How this interacts with existing flows:
- Existing onboard hooks continue to record per-model changelog fragments unchanged. The new emitter appends a structured "rollback_annotation" field to those fragments when the onboarding job reaches a nominated stability gate (configurable).
- The compact indexer reads fragments (S3/GS compatible) and produces a single JSONL.gz index that the console reads. The index is additive: consumers that don't opt in will be unaffected.

Review & feedback timeline (condensed):
- 2024-04-11: initial draft opened. Included proto/schema and indexer prototype. CI failing on flakiness in the Python test harness. (CI: fail)
- 2024-04-12: @Liam Chen: requested clearer fail-safe behavior if indexer encounters malformed fragments; asked to add a retry/backoff and a poison-file metric.
  - Response: added retry logic (backoff capped at 30s) and emitted metrics (indexer.malformed_fragments_total).
- 2024-04-14: @Priya Kapoor: asked for perf bounds and for the indexer to avoid loading full payloads into memory. Also requested a compact schema example in docs.
  - Response: switched to streaming JSONL parsing in the Go indexer and added memory usage tests. Updated docs with schema examples and a snippet showing how to query the index from the Console API.
- 2024-04-16: @Ethan Rivera: asked to ensure rollback annotations are cryptographically bound to onboard provenance (trace id + signer). Concerned about auditability for Private installs.
  - Response: added an optional signer field (kms_key_id) in the emitter; by default signer is empty for hosted but the field is available for Private deployments. Documented the behavior and added a test that verifies signer injection when env var is present.
- 2024-04-17: CI rerun; two minor lint fixes and a test timeout adjustment. (CI: pass)

CI status and flakiness notes:
- Initial CI run failed due to test harness timing assumptions. Subsequent runs pass. The indexer's unit tests include a lightweight fixture to simulate malformed fragments and validate metric emission. CI summary: build ✓, unit-tests ✓, lint ✓, integration (index smoke) ✓.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for emitter semantics and signer injection (tests/onboard/test_rollback_annotations.py).
notes: Merged after approvals from all reviewers. The change is additive and guarded by feature flags: ONBOARD_ENABLE_ROLLBACK_ANNOTATIONS and RELEASE_COMPACT_INDEX. We will flip the flags for internal staging and run a 2-week observation window before enabling in production. Backfill: a migration script (not in this PR) will create index entries for the last 90 days of fragments.
